summary: The Roar reports that Rugby Australia is close to naming World Rugby's director of high-performance Peter Horne as its new director of high-performance, ahead of former Sydney University, Australian Sevens and Harlequins director of rugby Billy Millard. Horne's close working relationship with Joe Schmidt could help RA land Schmidt as the next Wallabies coach to replace Eddie Jones. RA is also trying to bring Ireland's David Nucifora on board as a consultant despite his earlier doubts about returning.
one_line: Rugby Australia is set to name World Rugby's Peter Horne as high-performance director, a move that could help recruit Joe Schmidt as Wallabies coach.
key_facts: Peter Horne, World Rugby's director of high-performance, is set to be named Rugby Australia's new director of high-performance, likely within the next week.
Horne is believed to have edged out Billy Millard, former Sydney University, Australian Sevens and Harlequins director of rugby, for the role.
Horne joined World Rugby in 2015 as a general manager of high-performance before moving into his current role, and briefly worked at Saracens as a general manager.

The next Wallabies coach will report to Horne, who will oversee all of Australia's men's and women's high-performance programs and 'integrate' them, including centralising Super Rugby high-performance programs.
RA wants the new Wallabies coach set in stone by the start of Super Rugby, to replace Eddie Jones.
RA chief executive Phil Waugh said, 'It's the biggest job on my leadership team in terms of the impact it has on the general sentiment around the game.'

Joe Schmidt, the 58-year-old 2018 World Rugby coach of the year, worked alongside Horne at World Rugby after leaving Ireland following the 2019 World Cup, and is understood to be interested in the Wallabies job.
Schmidt coached Ireland for six years, took them to the top of World Rugby's rankings, and joined the All Blacks ahead of last year's Rugby Championship after a stint with the Blues.
Schmidt and Jason Ryan helped Ian Foster's All Blacks reach the final of this year's World Cup after wins over Ireland and Argentina in the knockout stages.
Dan McKellar, Stephen Larkham, Andy Friend and Ian Foster remain interested in the Wallabies role.
David Nucifora, Ireland's long-time director of high-performance, said last year 'I don't think it'd be wise to revisit' RA, and plans to leave Ireland after next year's Olympics.
RA is understood to be trying to get Nucifora on board as a consultant when he wraps up with Ireland; he was never in the running for the director role.
